description: What must be proven before the first controlled organization pilot (ADR 0038). Statuses are not written here: scripts/pilot-readiness.mjs computes them from the test results of the commit being assessed. A capability is GREEN only when every proof ran and passed and no open limitation is linked to it.

proofs.test: forces row-level security with a tenant policy on every table that has an organization
shows a tenant exactly its own rows in every tenant table
refuses writes that name another tenant, even with its identifiers
fails closed on scope misuse and on a tenant role that could bypass row security
keeps one tenant from reaching or overwriting another tenant’s objects
keeps checkpoints inside their tenant, their lease and their version order
fails closed on manifests with a bad signature, key, subject or profile
fails closed on unknown or missing manifest versions
pins released versions: a mutated version fails startup, new versions register
never serves a stored version it cannot verify
refuses bundles this release cannot interpret, even with a matching digest
issues one signed, operation-bound grant for an allowed in-scope operation
refuses forged, expired, mismatched and replayed-while-running grants before any work
denies requests that are unconfigured, out of scope, mismatched or under-granted
pauses with a payload-bound expiring approval, then executes exactly once after approval
expires unanswered approvals, cancels the run and rejects late decisions
only ever keeps or tightens the platform decision
lets exactly one of two simultaneous approval decisions succeed
12. stops for reconciliation when a connector times out after the remote system may have accepted (manual reconciliation)
caps output at what the run may still use, then denies and audits
serializes concurrent reservations, so the last tokens are granted once
lets only the runtime holding a running run reserve, and settle only its own reservations
makes no model call once the limit is reached, and fails the run
1. recovers when the runtime dies during a model call (recovery)
never prints, serializes or inspects a secret value
reads Vault KV v2 under the organization path and trusts nothing else
gives the credential once, to an execution runtime holding the exact grant
refuses another tenant, another grant, another operation and a forged grant
stores no credential in any table: events, audit, alerts, webhooks or quality results
gives the key only to the runtime holding a running run that names the provider
still fails closed for employee-held keys
runs a real runtime on the brokered key without the key reaching any durable record
8. fails closed when the secret store is unavailable (fail closed, then safe retry)
checks out a private repository without the credential reaching anything but git
checks out nothing once the lease is revoked
clones a private repository and leaves no trace of the credential
never falls back to an anonymous clone
redacts the credential from git errors, output and evidence
cleans up after a crash: partial checkout removed, lease ended, grant closed
builds a locked-down docker run with only the given environment
builds a locked-down egress proxy that runs only the mounted proxy script
writes files inside the workspace only, never through links or into .git
forwards plain HTTP and CONNECT tunnels to allowed hosts only
refuses allowed names that resolve to blocked or unknown addresses
11. never starts the sandbox when the egress proxy fails to start (fail closed)
11b. never starts the sandbox when its private network cannot be created, or no proxy is configured

operationalProofs.test: runs project scripts with no network, no secrets and a read-only root filesystem
lets networked grants reach only their allowed hosts, through the egress proxy
runs real Chromium against the allowed QA host and nothing else

proofs.test: lets runtime B finish the run runtime A abandoned, without repeating the external action
fails closed when the stored checkpoint was altered
reaps abandoned runs nothing can continue, and stops endless recovery
1. recovers when the runtime dies during a model call (recovery)
2. recovers when the runtime dies immediately before a tool (recovery)
3. reuses the recorded result when the runtime dies after a governed action succeeded (idempotent reuse)
4. reuses the execution result when the runtime dies after the operation but before its checkpoint (idempotent reuse)
5. recovers when the runtime dies during an artifact upload, and removes what it left (recovery)
6a. lets active runs continue after the control plane restarts (recovery)
6b. stops for reconciliation when the control plane dies while dispatching a write (manual reconciliation)
6c. closes dispatches a stopped control plane left open, without its runtime asking
7. closes the operation a stopped runtime was in the middle of, and never runs it twice (fail closed)
cleans up after a crash: partial checkout removed, lease ended, grant closed
10. rides out lost database connections (safe retry)
12b. treats a server error and an unreadable answer to a write as unknown, and a refusal as final
stores uploaded bytes outside PostgreSQL and registers only what it verified
enforces hashes and sizes on upload and refuses runtimes that do not hold the run
retrieves content only for the right person, briefly, and only if the hash still holds
enforces retention: bytes are deleted and the lifecycle is recorded
signs S3 requests exactly as AWS Signature Version 4 specifies
authorizes exactly one object, accepts it only after reading it back, and serves it
removes and records bytes that are not what was declared, however they got there
authorizes only execution runtimes, for recorded grants, allowed types and sizes, within the run quota
takes the bytes on a signed, single-purpose path and checks them before storing
stores a failed run with its trace, screenshot, console output and report, each with a retention class
collects traces and screenshots within limits and nothing else
9. keeps the run going when the artifact store is unavailable, and stores again when it returns (safe retry)
is one connected trace per run, named by the platform’s own identifiers, with no content in it
counts refusals, conflicts and corrupt checkpoints
keeps only listed attributes with identifier-like values
never lets an exporter or a collector fail the work being measured
bounds metric labels and series, and renders counters, gauges and histograms
exports spans and metrics as OTLP over HTTPS, and drops them when the collector is down
serves metrics only to a caller with the operator token
serves metrics only to a caller with the operator token
covers every role version with at least one scenario
runs a task through the real platform, approves what the task allows, and grades it
fails a task whose gate misses, whatever the score: a denied action is out of scope
gives every role at least one quality task
gates every quality task on staying in scope and finishing the run
runs validate-story end to end with governed reads, execution and approved writes
names no role outside the catalog, except the documented legacy QA compatibility

limitations.summary: The S3-compatible adapter is proven against the AWS signing example and a simulated bucket that checks signatures, not against a live S3, GCS or MinIO service.
limitations.beforePilot: Run an upload, direct upload, retrieval and retention pass against the pilot bucket.

limitations.summary: The Vault provider is proven against a simulated KV v2 API, not against a live Vault.
limitations.beforePilot: Resolve one connector secret and one model key through the pilot Vault.

limitations.summary: Employee-held model keys are refused (fail closed). The desktop-local runtime that would use them is designed, not built.
limitations.beforePilot: Pilot with organization-managed model credentials only.

limitations.summary: git.checkout runs on the execution runtime's host behind the egress proxy, not inside the sandbox container. It executes no repository code.
limitations.beforePilot: Run execution runtimes on hosts dedicated to the pilot organization.

limitations.summary: A run abandoned by its runtime is picked up after its lease expires: up to ten minutes.
limitations.beforePilot: Tell pilot users; alert on af_runtime_leases{state="expired"}.

limitations.summary: Checkpoint bodies hold conversation content and are not encrypted by the application; they rely on database encryption at rest and row-level security.
limitations.beforePilot: Confirm encryption at rest on the pilot database.

limitations.summary: An artifact is read fully into memory to verify its hash before it is served or accepted: up to 128 MiB per request.
limitations.beforePilot: Size the control plane's memory for concurrent trace downloads.

limitations.summary: Artifact download, model credentials and source-control connections have APIs but no screens in the web or desktop applications.
limitations.beforePilot: Give pilot administrators the API runbook.

limitations.summary: Writes with an unknown outcome are reconciled by an administrator through the API; there is no screen and no notification beyond the metric and audit event.
limitations.beforePilot: Alert on af_action_reconciliations_total{event="required"} and document the runbook.

limitations.summary: The OTLP exporter and the Prometheus endpoints are proven in tests, not against a live collector or scraper.
limitations.beforePilot: Point the pilot deployment at its collector and confirm one run's trace arrives whole.

limitations.summary: No dashboards or alert rules are shipped; the metrics catalog is the input for them.
limitations.beforePilot: Create alerts for run failures, lease expiry, budget denials, store and secret failures, and reconciliations.

limitations.summary: Live model-quality evaluation spends real tokens, so it runs weekly or by hand, not on every commit. Governance evaluations run on every commit.
limitations.beforePilot: Run the model-quality workflow for the pilot's model and review the scores.

limitations.summary: There is no MCP client: tools are the runtime's own implementations of catalog tool definitions.
limitations.beforePilot: None for the engineering roles shipped.

limitations.summary: There is no Skill Runtime: skills are catalog data that shape the prompt and name the tools; they do not execute.
limitations.beforePilot: None for the engineering roles shipped.
